text: Body interrupts the dialogue. They added this extra measure of caution. That is, at the Mac layer, let's have a counter that sets the node whether the channel is busy or idle. Essentially, okay. If the node is greater than zero, at the Mac layer we say the channel is busy. If the node is equal to zero, then at the Mac layer we say the channel is idle. So what do we have here? What we have, if you think about it, is the fact that we have a double sensing function, one acting at the physical layer and one acting at the Mac layer. The sensing function at the physical layer is the one that we explained earlier, right? That is physically you sense if there is power on the channel. There's something physical, it's power, okay? Something concrete. So at the physical layer, by sensing the actual level of power energy that is on the channel, you can say at the physical layer the channel idle or channel busy. Now we have an extra additional sensing function that is at the Mac layer and it's called virtual sensing function because it's not something physical, right? You don't sense the power, but what you do is to set a counter, reset a value, and then you say.
